title: Judicial Overreach vs. Separation of Powers in Tribunal Appointments
prelims_pointers: Tribunals were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 (Article 323A and 323B).
Supreme Court has repeatedly struck down provisions of the Tribunals Reforms Act for violating judicial independence.
Article 50 directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services.

mains_perspective.context: Recent controversies regarding executive appointments and vacancies in appellate tribunals highlight friction between judicial oversight and executive discretion.
mains_perspective.key_arguments: Pro-judiciary arguments emphasize institutional integrity and specialized justice. Counter-arguments point to democratic accountability and judicial encroachment into policy domains.
mains_perspective.way_forward: Establish an independent National Tribunals Commission to streamline appointments and insulate administrative bodies from bureaucratic delays.

title: Climate Finance and the New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG)
prelims_pointers: NCQG is established under the Paris Agreement to set a new financial floor above the previous $100 billion/year target.
Principle of Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) guides UNFCCC negotiations.
India's updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) focus on non-fossil energy capacity.

mains_perspective.context: Developing nations face massive capital constraints in meeting net-zero transitions without jeopardizing poverty eradication mandates.
mains_perspective.key_arguments: Developed nations must provide public, grant-based climate finance rather than high-interest loans that exacerbate sovereign debt burdens.
mains_perspective.way_forward: Leverage blended finance models, green bonds, and technology transfer mechanisms while holding historic emitters accountable.
